scene_description: A small tiled bedroom viewed from an elevated corner, with a foreground bed, shelving and a cabinet on the back wall, two floor lamps, an open doorway, and a white furniture panel at right.
initial_target_observations: The initial doorway is largely a dark vertical opening with only a very thin pale strip at its right edge. It lacks the broad, visibly open wooden door leaf and prominent foreground occlusion in the reference.
candidate_target_observations: The candidate adds a pale wooden door leaf projecting into the room beside the dark doorway. Its angled silhouette is more recognizable than the initial strip, but it is much narrower and less prominent than the reference leaf and has only faint panel detail. It does not create the same extensive foreground occlusion.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The candidate door reads as an angled leaf at the opening, though its apparent size, angle and position differ substantially from the reference. The bed, shelves, cabinet and lamps retain a plausible general arrangement, but their apparent contact and hidden geometry cannot be established from the images.
new_visible_defects: No definite new defect is visible; the new door remains undersized in the image relative to the reference.
other_changes: The rest of the candidate closely resembles the initial image. Compared with the reference, the viewpoint is wider and more frontal, the bed dominates the lower foreground, the right white furniture is simplified, and surfaces and lighting are flatter. The reference has stronger warm lamp illumination, a mottled floor or rug, and more visible wood grain and door paneling.

evidence.description: A broad paneled wooden door leaf projects into the foreground and obscures part of the room.
The dark doorway has only a narrow pale edge rather than a clearly visible open leaf.
A narrow angled pale door leaf is now visible against the dark opening, but it is much less prominent than in the reference.
The white shelf and cabinet sit between two lamps, with warm light on the tiled wall.
The shelf, cabinet and lamps are similarly arranged, but lighting and materials are comparatively uniform.
The large foreground bed and simplified white panel at right differ in framing and detail from the reference.

uncertainty: The door comparison is based on rendered silhouettes from different viewpoints; the exact door dimensions, hinge connections, mesh contact and collisions cannot be confirmed from RGB images. The target is judged partial because a leaf is visible but its reference-like prominence and occlusion remain absent.
